entries.claim: The pinned Latin Mass data independently corroborate the component's substantive Latin and expose accidental editorial variants for collation.

locator.section: In vigilia Ascensionis; Secreta; left column continuing at upper right

entries.claim: In the Ascension Vigil, the page prints Suscipe, Domine, fidelium preces through ad caelestem gloriam transeamus (w001–w017), continuing from the left column to the upper right, and the Per Dominum cue. The supplied common conclusion (w018–w038), its audible final clause and separate Amen (w039) retain their distinct wording and ritual-boundary sources.

locator.section: RG 480–481, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ordo Missae rubric and chant formula after the secrets

entries.claim: The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a: Father-directed common conclusion

entries.claim: Rubricae generales 115 a prints the full twenty-one-word Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum Filium tuum conclusion through per omnia saecula saeculorum and following Amen. It supports the supplied wording at w018–w038 and the separate w039 Amen after the proper page’s Per Dominum cue. Reader accents, ligatures, colon after tuum and uppercase Qui are declared editorial accidentals, not exact typography from this rubric. This use does not assign the response performer or prayer voice.

The cited page prints this prayer’s proper body and the abbreviated conclusion “Per Dóminum”. The full common conclusion and Amen are supplied separately in the reader, with its own accentuation, capitalization and punctuation.

witnesses.independence_basis: Pinned upstream Latin data maintained independently of this corpus; used as a derived comparison witness, not as the controlling edition.

The proper prayer is directly collated against the identified page image of the Benziger Brothers 1962 editio iuxta typicam. The complete MR transcript expands the Per Dominum cue with the 21-word common conclusion and following Amen at w018–w039. Rubricae generales 115a, printed p. xvii, supports the common wording; the expanded reading retains the reader accents, ligatures, colon after tuum and uppercase Qui declared in the transcript, rather than claiming those accidentals from the proper-page cue. This composite reading is not a further independent witness.

collation.recension: The 1962 component in the approved Benziger printing, with declared shared expansions and house orthography
